instructions: Think about your child over the past month. For each moment, pick the ONE answer that sounds most like your child right now, even if more than one fits. There are no wrong answers: every choice is a strength.
frequency_stem: In the past month, how often does your child...

scenarios.prompt: A free afternoon with no plans. Your child is most likely to...

options.text: curl up with a book, or write a story or comic
work on a puzzle, a code, or a game with lots of rules
draw, design a Lego build, or rearrange their room

scenarios.prompt: At co-op or a group class, your child lights up during...

options.text: anything hands-on: experiments, crafts, games that move
music time, singing, or anything with a rhythm
group work, and getting to know the other kids

scenarios.prompt: On a hike or a walk in the woods, your child...

options.text: goes quiet and seems to enjoy their own thoughts
spots tracks, birds or plants and wants to know what they are
asks big questions, like why God made the world this way

scenarios.prompt: When something exciting happens, your child wants to...

options.text: tell you every detail, start to finish
show you, act it out, or rebuild it
think it over first and talk about it later

scenarios.prompt: On a long car trip, your child passes the time by...

options.text: tracking the miles, the map, or the time left
listening to music, singing, or making up songs
watching for animals, farms and changes in the land

scenarios.prompt: At church, your child is most drawn to...

options.text: the art and the building, or drawing what they hear
the people: friends, older folks, the greeters
the Bible lesson, and asking questions about it later

scenarios.prompt: At the end of the day, your child is most likely to...

options.text: read late, or tell you a long story from their day
listen to music, hum, or sing to themselves
ask about God, heaven, or what is right and wrong

scenarios.prompt: On family game night, your child...

options.text: wants to master the strategy and keep score
cares most that everyone is having fun together
enjoys it, then wants some quiet time alone afterward

scenarios.prompt: Given a free Saturday and some supplies, your child would...

options.text: sketch a plan and build something that looks just right
build, take apart or fix something with real tools
plant something, care for a pet, or set up a bug habitat

scenarios.prompt: When cousins or friends visit, your child...

options.text: entertains everyone with jokes and stories
makes sure no one is left out and plans the fun
takes them outside to explore the yard or the creek

scenarios.prompt: With a school project, your child...

options.text: makes a plan, a list or a chart first
wants to build a model or do a demonstration
wants to dig into the why behind it, and what it means

scenarios.prompt: Alone in their room, your child is most likely to...

options.text: draw, design, or build something detailed
play an instrument, sing, or make up music
journal, read, or simply think

frequency.text: read, write, or tell stories for fun
solve puzzles, work with numbers, or ask how things work
draw, map, or build things they picture in their head
build, fix, or make things with their hands
sing, play music, or notice sounds and rhythms
help others, or look for ways to do things together
want time alone to think things through
notice, collect, or ask about plants, animals or the outdoors
ask big questions about God, life, or right and wrong
